data.raw_response:
=== Morphological Assessment Form ===
A. Leaf Arrangement & Architecture
    1. Leaf relative position (alternate / opposite / whorled): alternate (leaves are attached singly at different nodes along the stem in an alternating pattern)
    2. Leaf spacing (clustered / distal): distal (leaves are spaced out along the stem rather than clustered together)
B. Leaf Complexity
    3. Leaf complexity (simple / compound): simple (each leaf blade is undivided and attaches to the stem via a petiole)
    4. Compound leaf type, ONLY if leaf complexity is compound (odd-pinnate / even-pinnate): N/A
    5. Number of leaflets (integer estimate 2, 4, 8, …): N/A
    6. Leaflet arrangement (opposite / alternate / subopposite): N/A
C. Leaf Morphology
    7. Leaf margin (entire / toothed) AND if toothed (dentate, serrate, etc.): entire (the leaf margins are smooth without teeth or serrations)
    8. Leaf shape (elliptic, obovate, lanceolate, etc.): cordate (the leaves are distinctly heart-shaped with a deep notch at the base)
    9. Leaf apex (acute, obtuse, acuminate): acute (the tip of the leaf tapers to a distinct point)
    10. Leaf base (rounded, cordate, cuneate): cordate (the base of the leaf is heart-shaped with a deep sinus)
    11. Venation type (pinnate / palmate / parallel): palmate (several main veins radiate from the base of the leaf blade)
    12. Secondary veins (visibility, spacing, number): clearly visible and prominent, arching from the primary veins towards the margin
    13. Leaf surface features (glabrous, shiny, dull, rugose): shiny (the leaf surface reflects light, appearing glossy)
    14. Leaf surface trichomes (present / absent): present (fine, short hairs are visible along the leaf margins, particularly in the close-up images)
    15. Petiole length (short / long): long (the petioles are slender and noticeably longer than the width of the leaf base)
    16. Petiole features (winged / grooved / terete): terete (the petioles appear cylindrical and round in cross-section)
D. Stem & Shoot Traits
    17. Stem type, may not be visible (woody / herbaceous): herbaceous (the stem appears thin, green, and flexible, characteristic of a young seedling)
    18. Stem trichomes (present / absent): absent (the stem appears smooth without visible hairs)
    19. Stem color: green (the stem is a uniform green color)
    20. Stem texture (smooth / ridged / lenticellate): smooth (the stem surface appears smooth and even)
E. Other Visible Seedling Traits
    21. Stipules, sometimes visible only in close-up images (present / absent): absent (no stipules are visible at the base of the petioles)
    22. Latex, rarely visible but extremely diagnostic when present (present / not observed): not observed
    23. Pulvinus, for Fabaceae family only (present / absent): absent (no distinct swollen joint or pulvinus is visible at the leaf base)
    24. Tendrils (present / absent): absent (no tendrils are visible on the seedling)
F. Notes: The seedling exhibits heterophylly, with some leaves being cordate (heart-shaped) and others appearing more elliptic/lanceolate. There is visible damage on some leaves, including holes and missing sections of the margin.
